```sql
WITH page AS (
  SELECT a.id,
         a.created_at
    FROM audit_log a
   WHERE a.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
     AND (%(table_name)s::text IS NULL OR a.table_name = %(table_name)s)
     AND (%(row_id)s::uuid IS NULL OR a.row_id = %(row_id)s)
     AND a.created_at >= %(from)s
     AND a.created_at <  %(to)s
   ORDER BY a.created_at DESC, a.id DESC
   LIMIT %(limit)s OFFSET %(offset)s
)
SELECT a.id,
       a.tenant_id,
       a.table_name,
       a.row_id,
       a.action,
       a.old_data,
       a.new_data,
       a.actor_id,
       a.is_system,
       a.created_at
  FROM page p
  JOIN audit_log a
    ON a.id = p.id
   AND a.created_at = p.created_at
 ORDER BY a.created_at DESC, a.id DESC
```

Deze "deferred join" sorteert en pagineert alleen de smalle kolommen (id, created_at) en haalt de brede `old_data`/`new_data`-waarden pas op voor de rijen op de pagina. De winst is het grootst als er geen index op `(tenant_id, created_at, id)` is, of bij grote OFFSET-waarden. Zonder EXPLAIN ANALYZE op jullie data en schema kan ik dit niet bevestigen.
